findings.title: Only `pre-advance` is designed; the other gates have no insertion point or status
findings.description:
The config defines `pre-slice-plan`, `pre-tasks`, `pre-implementation` and `pre-advance`, but only `pre-advance` has a design.

- **Insertion point:** "Gate insertion point" describes one branch, between Priority 5 and Priority 6. A `pre-tasks` gate must fire while the slice is `needs-tasks`, and `pre-implementation` when a task file exists with tasks unchecked. Neither is mentioned.
- **Status values:** `pending-review` is defined as "tasks complete, review gate configured, no review artifact present". That cannot represent a missing slice-design or task review.
- **Which review:** neither `pending-review` nor `review-failed` carries the transition or reviewType, so a runner cannot tell which review agent to route to without parsing the rationale.
- **Slice scope:** Anticipated Slice 2 covers only the "complete" case, so `pre-tasks` and `pre-implementation` belong to no slice.
- **Count:** "V1 implements only the four slice-level transitions" is wrong; with `pre-slice-plan` deferred there are three.

Either cut v1 to `pre-advance` only and remove the other keys, or design each insertion point and add a `gate`/`reviewType` field to the status.

findings.title: The "stable recommendation vocabulary" the design depends on does not exist
findings.description:
The document says consumers can act "without parsing recommendation strings" and that the gate must "only add new `recommendation` string values" to a stable vocabulary. `NextAction.recommendation` is free-form prose in the current code.

- **Existing values are prose:** examples are `` `Advance to slice ${nextEntry.index}: ${nextEntry.name}` `` and `` `Continue implementation — ${remaining} task(s) remaining` `` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:240,253`).
- **No `advance` token:** the `workflow.auto_advance` paragraph reasons about "an `advance` recommendation", which is not a value the code emits.
- **Mixed field:** adding `"review"` and `"blocked"` makes one field hold both sentences and enum tokens.
- **Wrong surface:** `SliceStatus.status` is returned by `getStatus()`, not in `NextAction`, so the new statuses are not visible to a `workflow_next` consumer.
- **Constraint conflict:** the fix is a discriminant on `NextAction` (for example `action: 'review' | 'blocked' | 'advance' | …` plus `reviewType`). That contradicts the stated constraint "must not change the `NextAction` return type".

The Amoeba integration cannot be built deterministically until this is resolved.

findings.title: Verdict, threshold and `review_unknown_as` rules contradict each other
findings.description:
- **`review_unknown_as` values:** the doc uses `"fail"` (config block), `"concern"` (Technical Considerations, singular against the `concerns` threshold), and "treats it as pending" (Slice status extension). The value set is never enumerated.
- **UNKNOWN under the default:** with a file present, an unreadable verdict maps to `review-failed` under the rules but `pending-review` under the status definition. The sample rationale would report "verdict FAIL" for a file that has no verdict.
- **Threshold ordering:** "`CONCERNS` clears if `review_threshold = "concerns"` or lower" implies a value below `concerns`. Only `pass` and `concerns` appear, and the enum is not stated.
- **Enabled with no gates table:** `review_gates` is called "optional per-transition overrides", implying built-in gates. But "no gate is configured for the current transition" means advance. The doc does not say whether `review_enabled = true` alone gates anything, or what the default transition-to-reviewType map is.

The document needs a single decision table of verdict × threshold × unknown_as mapping to status. The Slice 2 test matrix cannot be written without it.

findings.title: `WorkflowNavigator` has no config access; "inherited without per-surface work" is false
findings.description:
`WorkflowNavigator` is a stateless class. `getNext(project: ProjectData)` takes no config and has no constructor dependencies. It is built as `new WorkflowNavigator()` at four call sites: `cli/commands/next.ts:26`, `cli/commands/status.ts:119`, and `mcp-server/tools/workflowTools.ts:154,200`. `ConsistencyChecker` takes only an introspector.

The gate needs resolved `workflow.review_*` values, including the worktree-scope chain the doc requests from 180. So either every call site resolves and injects config, or core introspection imports `ConfigManager` directly, which the project's dependency-inversion rule forbids. The doc specifies neither, and it also contradicts "no 160 interfaces change". It should define an injected `ReviewGatePolicy` value and list the call-site changes.

findings.title: Existing frontmatter parser cannot meet the stated failure-mode and contract requirements
findings.description:
The doc requires that a parse failure be named explicitly in the rationale. Three pieces of existing code prevent that:

- **`parseFrontmatter` hides the cause:** it "never throws" and returns `{found: false, data: {}}` for a permission error, a missing closing `---`, and no frontmatter alike.
- **`deriveSliceStatus` swallows errors:** its `catch {}` at `:494` returns `no-active-slice`.
- **`safeReaddir` hides directory errors:** an unreadable reviews directory looks the same as "no review".

The parser is also a flat line scanner that trims indentation and lets the last key win. The slice 300 schema has nested `criteria` and `provenance`. A nested `verdict:` or `score:` line under `criteria` would silently overwrite the top-level `verdict`, flipping the gate.

The design needs a review-specific reader that returns a discriminated result (`absent | unreadable(reason) | parsed(verdict)`) and reads only top-level keys or uses a real YAML parser. The tests need a fixture from an actual Squadron slice 300 artifact; no review artifact exists in this repo to validate against.

findings.title: Gate evaluation is placed in `WorkflowNavigator` but is needed by two components
findings.description:
Slice 2 puts the verdict/threshold logic in `WorkflowNavigator`. Slice 3 needs the same evaluation in `ConsistencyChecker` ("verdict does not clear the threshold"). As written, the logic is either duplicated or the checker depends on the navigator.

`WorkflowNavigator.ts` is also already over 500 lines against a ~300-line convention. The design should extract a pure `evaluateReviewGate(policy, artifact) → cleared | pending | failed(reason)` module that both consume. `documentDetector` should stay config-free: return all `NNN-review.*` matches and let the gate select by type, instead of passing "configured reviewType" into the detector.

findings.title: Multi-artifact selection rule is arbitrary and review freshness is unaddressed
findings.description:
"Lexicographically last filename (most recent by sort order)" is not recency. The pattern `NNN-review.{type}.{name}.md` has no date or sequence component, so the choice between two files is alphabetical by slug.

The doc also does not say whether a re-review overwrites the artifact or adds a file. If it overwrites, the multi-match rule is dead code. If it adds, the rule picks arbitrarily, and a stale PASS can outrank a newer FAIL.

Nothing ties a verdict to the reviewed state. A PASS written before later rework clears the gate indefinitely. Either state that as an accepted limitation or select by a frontmatter date field.

findings.title: ConsistencyChecker rule is retroactive and disagrees with the gate on severity
findings.description:
The rule fires for every slice "marked complete in the slice plan". Turning on `review_enabled` in an existing project will emit a warning for every historical slice that predates reviews, with no baseline or cutoff.

The rule also does not say which transition it checks (presumably `pre-advance` only) or what happens when that gate is not configured. A missing review is `warning` here but blocking in `getNext()`. A slice checked off in the plan despite `review-failed` is the real inconsistency, and the doc does not distinguish it.

findings.title: Overweight for v1: unenforced and unconsumed mechanisms
findings.description:
These can be cut or deferred against the project's "resist complexity" rule:

- **`score`:** it is "read and stored" with no consumer and no stated storage location, alongside an "enforcement switch" code path. Drop it until slice 301.
- **`criteria` / `provenance`:** "carried as opaque fields… preserved" is meaningless because CF never writes review artifacts. Do not read them.
- **`pre-slice-plan` key:** it is accepted in config while its logic is deferred. A configured gate that silently does nothing violates the doc's own fail-fast principle. Reject the key until it is implemented.
- **`review_unknown_as`:** a three-way policy knob for a malformed-artifact case. Hard-coding "blocks" removes the interaction matrix described in Technical Considerations.
- **`review_gates` table:** it needs a nested-config mechanism that `ConfigKeyDefinition` (scalar only) does not have. The doc defers that decision "to slice design time" even though it sits in the foundation slice. If v1 is `pre-advance` only, two scalar keys suffice and the nested-table problem goes away.

findings.title: Cascade renumbering is assigned to the wrong slice
findings.description: Slice 1 ("no gate logic yet") includes renumbering the `getNext()` priority comments, while Technical Considerations says it belongs with the gate branch. The cascade already has a "Priority 2.5", so fractional labels are tolerated. Do the renumbering in Slice 2 or skip it.
